answer: Gate standing on a bond posted by an unaffiliated underwriter drawn from a finite registry of out-of-band-proven parties, jointly slashed in onyx if the agent faults. A lone sparrow agent needs one real underwriter; a farm needs a distinct non-kin underwriter per clone, and each recruitment shrinks the honest pool by a measurable delta, so cost climbs super-linearly and cannot be pooled, since one underwriter backing correlated clones exposes shared control at settlement. Failure mode: colluding underwriters, bounded by capping backings per underwriter.
